data.hypothesis: The 16-byte SSE2 prefix scan can skip long initial ASCII runs, while the 8-byte word checks after the first mixed vector may skip later complete ASCII blocks that scalar suffix decoding would inspect byte by byte. The additional masks and mixed-block decoding may instead cost more on short or dense non-ASCII inputs. The combined program is unmeasured and must beat the parent's 39.978 µs mean; no additive gain is assumed.
data.notes: Both supplied source ideas are retained in one independently measured candidate. The prior measured means are 39.978 µs for 31112 and 57.505 µs for 1bef; they motivate the test but do not predict the combined result. The Gm1 catalog has no recorded trials and zero observed source diversity. Controller correctness and performance measurements are required.
transformations: Retained the bounded 16-byte SSE2 ASCII-prefix scan and its handoff at the first vector containing a high-bit byte.
Replaced scalar suffix processing with an 8-byte high-bit mask loaded using memcpy; decode mixed blocks by complete code point through the block boundary, then validate the bounded scalar tail.
Preserved the UTF-8 validity rules, run ABI, output, and conditional SSE2 compilation.
